note: Group russian_soviet, version 3. IMSLP (author categories plus an enumeration of all 1,620 solo-violin pages cross-checked against IMSLP nationality categories for Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Bulgarian, Romanian, Serbian, Croatian, Armenian, Georgian, Baltic, Azerbaijani) is thin for Soviet authors (copyright), so Soviet items rest on Open Library/Library of Congress records (title, publisher, year, page count only; contents NOT seen) and on ru.wikipedia. Could not reach RSL/NEB (HTTP 403), WorldCat, Google Books (HTTP 429) or notes.tarakanov.net; no scale/arpeggio book by Mostras, Yampolsky, Yankelevich, Garlitsky, Furer, Sibor or Stolyarsky was found, and none of them is on IMSLP as an author of studies. Levels of all Soviet items are guesses (no syllabus data) and should go to the blind graders. Auer's Graded Course: Books 5-7 are listed from the Book 1 preface and Open Library records (Book 5/6/7 text not seen); Books 1 and 8 were read in the archive.org scans. Christoskov rows 608/609 verified (titles, opus, dates correct; Bulgarian sources spell Hristoskov, dates 1917-2006). Overlaps with other files: Szałowski 6 Caprices is in concert_etudes (removed here); Barmas 'Die Lösung des geigentechnischen Problems' is in world_other at L5, but IMSLP describes a book with musical examples, so I list it in skipped as a treatise (owner to decide); Eliason Op. 12 and Dworzak Op. 1 are in concert_etudes. Kotek Op. 8, Gavrilov, Lvov and Yanshinov were flagged by central_european as 'Russian group' and are entered here. Already covered elsewhere and not repeated: Hřímalý Scale Studies, Jacobsen, Heifetz scale book, Flesch Russian edition, Polish authors in central_european.
